source:
@@U03657@@
Our mountains, our cities,
our shores and sea
are pleasing to him, the god,
and are lovely and bright.
We have no fogs or mist, no sunless haze,
and should one steal upon us,
a beam of sun and a breeze
clears us of these,
and the island is once again bright.
From on high he sees himself,
your brother god,
in a hundred statues,
as a youth, a giant, now great, now gentle.
We were the first, you know, in all the world,
to cast the gods in the noble form of man.

@@U03659@@
(To 荷蒙库鲁斯,)

@@U03660@@
Let them sing, let them boast.
To the sacred life-giving rays of the sun
such lifeless things are nothing.
They go on sculpting, casting, endlessly,
and once they have it in bronze
they think they've really got something.
And what comes of all this pride in the end?
These godly statues stand there so grand—
and an earthquake destroys them.
They've been melted down long since.
What is this earthly life,
even at its best,
but a weariness of the flesh!
The sea is the proper element for life.
I'll be 普罗透斯-Dolphin now,
and carry you into the eternal waters.

@@U03661@@
(He transforms himself.)

@@U03662@@
There, that’s done.
Up on my back, now.
translation:
@@U03657@@
我们的山，我们的城市，
我们的海岸和大海
神所喜悦的，
并且可爱又明亮。
我们没有雾气，没有没有阳光的薄雾，
如果有人偷袭我们，
一束阳光和一阵微风
清除我们这些，
岛屿再次变得明亮。
他从高处看到自己，
你的神兄弟，
在一百个雕像中，
少年时，巨人时，伟大时，温柔时。
你知道，我们是世界上第一个，
将众神塑造成高贵的人形。

@@U03659@@
（致荷蒙库鲁斯）

@@U03660@@
让他们歌唱，让他们夸耀。
献给赋予生命的神圣阳光
这种没有生命的东西算不了什么。
他们不断地雕刻、铸造，
一旦他们有了青铜色
他们认为自己确实有所作为。
所有这些骄傲最终会带来什么？
这些神圣的雕像矗立在那里，如此宏伟——
地震就把他们毁灭了。
它们早已被融化了。
这尘世的生活是什么，
即使在最好的状态下，
而是肉体的疲倦！
海洋是生命最适宜的元素。
我现在将成为普罗透斯-海豚，
并带你进入永恒之水。

@@U03661@@
（他改变了自己。）

@@U03662@@
到了这里，就完成了。
现在，在我的背上。
